jobs.title: Director, Engineering and Procurement, AI Fabric
jobs.description:
Req Id:
432862

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

Additional Information

Position Type:
Management

Job Status:
Regular - Full Time

Job Location:
Canada : Alberta : Calgary

Work Arrangement:
Hybrid

Application Deadline:
10/30/2026

For work arrangements that are ‘Hybrid’, successful candidates must be based in Canada and report to a set Bell office for a minimum of 3 days a week. Recognizing the importance of work-life balance, Bell offers flexibility in work hours based on the business needs.

Please apply directly online to be considered for this role. Applications through email will not be accepted.

We know that caring for our team members is at the heart of a healthy, positive and thriving workplace. As part of our team, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive compensation package that includes a competitive salary and a wide range of benefits to support the well-being of you and your family. As soon as you join us, you'll be eligible for medical, dental, vision and mental health benefits that you can tailor to your specific needs. Plus, as a Bell team member, you'll enjoy a 35% discount on our services and access exclusive offers from our partners.

At Bell, we are proud of our focus on fostering an inclusive and accessible workplace where all team members feel valued, respected, supported, and that they belong.

Bell is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise. We also want to make sure that everyone has an equal opportunity to join our team. We encourage individuals who may require accommodations during the hiring process to let us know. For a confidential inquiry, email your recruiter or recruitment@bell.ca to make arrangements. If you have questions or feedback regarding accessibility at Bell, we invite you to complete the Accessibility feedback form or visit our Accessibility page for other ways to contact us.

Artificial intelligence may be used to assess parts of your application. Please review our privacy policy (see Phenom for details) to learn more about how we collect, use, and disclose your personal information.

jobs.title: Director, North America Finance Business Partner
jobs.description:
Magellan Aerospace is a global, integrated aerospace company that provides complex assemblies and systems solutions to aircraft and engine manufacturers, and defence and space agencies worldwide. At Magellan we have over 80 years of collective knowledge and experience in the aerospace industry, and believe one truth: People create value.

Employees are our greatest resource in working towards a successful future, and together we build professional relationships that thrive. We know that personal development is fundamental to the success of every individual and invest in our employees.

When you are part of Magellan, you are part of the team!

Position Summary

Magellan Aerospace, Corporate has an exciting opportunity for a Director, North America Finance Business Partner.
Reporting to the Vice President, North American Operations and the Chief Financial Officer, the successful incumbent will be responsible for reviewing and supporting divisional reporting, forecasting, budgeting, strategic planning, business cases as well as other finance-related activities for all the North American divisions. The Individual will act as a trusted advisor to the Vice President, North American Operations, providing insightful analysis, financial advice, and business analytics to drive efficiencies and improve business performances and will liaise with the corporate finance department. The Director, North America Finance Business Partner will provide relationship management and technical financial counsel to the business units while ensuring that adherence to all regulations and guidelines.

Annual Salary Range: $115,000 to $140,000

Vacancy Reason: Replacement

Essential Responsibilities

Management Reporting

Review and provide support for all financial management reporting for the business unit.
Review and analyze monthly and year-to-date business unit financial reporting packages.
Develop regular reporting and analysis for management team, including key metrics reports, and conduct ad hoc financial analysis as required.
Support the annual budget plan development and process for the business units.
Provide on-going financial modeling and analysis expertise to management team as needed.
Support the 12 month financial modeling and analysis to support the development of long-term initiatives and business plans.
Lead the Regional financial consolidation and analysis.

Cash and Risk Management

Assess on-going cash activities for maximum efficiency.
Analyze and optimize cash flow forecasting.
Assist in developing business plans for strategic initiatives, major capital expenses and/or acquisitions as appropriate.
Assist in analyzing strategic plan financial data.

Accounting and Financial Controls

Develop a review process to ensure that finance and operations meet divisional and corporate targets.
Benchmark key division metrics against internal and external sources.

Human Capital Management

Provide financial support service and expertise for divisional operation.
Support the divisional finance staff by providing financial analysis and knowledge.
Ensure that the finance team delivers the highest standard of cross-departmental teamwork.

Position Requirements

Accounting degree or equivalent.
10 years of experience in Finance and Accounting and /or Finance Planning & Analysis.
Strong communication skills.
Relationship management.
Technical and functional expertise.
Problem solving.
Risk Management.

Why Magellan?

Competitive salary.
Attractive benefits package.
Generous Company Pension Plan.
Positive work-life balance.
Excellent career progression opportunities.
Employee Assistance Program.
On-site gym.
Free parking.

Magellan Aerospace is committed to an inclusive working environment and equal opportunities for all. We welcome all applications without regard to social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation, national origin or religious belief, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state/province, or local law.

If you require an accommodation during the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodation), please let your Human Resources point of contact know and we will work with you, to the best of our ability to meet your needs.

Magellan Aerospace respects the privacy and confidentiality of personal information provided by candidates and shall not disclose to any external parties unless legislated.

Magellan may use an approved Artificial Intelligence (AI) note-taking tool to support the initial screening stage of its recruitment and selection process. All AI use is performed in accordance with Magellan’s privacy policies. Personal information associated with any job application will not be shared with or retained by any third party. Magellan the ultimate discretion to determine which applications proceed through the initial screening process.

jobs.title: Associate Vice President, Corporate Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

KPMG Corporate Finance Inc. is the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC)-regulated entity through which KPMG LLP provides investment banking services in Canada. KPMG Corporate Finance services are principally comprised of merger, acquisition and divestiture services and financing services, including raising debt and equity capital. We offer independent financial advisory and investment banking services to both private and public companies.

With over 100 professionals across Canada and a global network of 3,000+ bankers in 160 offices, we combine local execution expertise with global reach. KPMG Corporate Finance is consistently ranked the #1 mid-market investment bank in Canada.

For more information click here

As an experienced Associate Vice President, Corporate Finance, you will report to our Vice Presidents and Managing Directors. You are a self-starter who has an interest in mergers and acquisitions and capital markets and will bring your experience to deliver transactions for our clients.

What You Will Do

Conduct market and industry research, detailed financial analysis and business valuations.
Draft pitch books, teasers, confidential information memorandums (CIM) and other Merger & Acquisition documentation.
Assume responsibility for the day-to-day execution and delivery of service on a range of corporate finance projects.
Assist in the identification of potential acquisition targets, purchasers and/or investors.
Assess the business environment and key drivers specific to the company and its sector.
Prepare and review financial models.
Manage, mentor and train junior corporate finance professionals.
Undertake engagement and practice management responsibilities, including billings and adherence to professional practice requirements.
Lead proactive business development and deal initiation activities.

This role provides significant learning opportunities and increasing responsibility over time. At times, business needs arise, and employees are required and agree to work beyond their normal workday or work week to fulfill the accountabilities required for their job. Likewise, employees need time to devote to personal matters, and our approach to flexibility provides for this.

What You Bring To The Role

Post-secondary degree in finance, commerce, business, accounting, economics, or other related field.
3 - 5 years of relevant post-graduate experience, in corporate finance, or a related field e.g. transaction advisory, investment banking, commercial/corporate banking, private equity, management consulting, or corporate development.
Proven track record of project initiation/execution in a fast-paced professional setting.
Strong technical finance proficiency, including knowledge of financial statements and general accounting principles.
Demonstrated experience or ability in training and developing junior staff members.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Must be willing to travel within and across Canada.
Ability to execute complex deliverables on a timely basis while managing competing priorities.
Attention to detail with excellent organizational skills and an ability to solve complex technical problems.
Collaborative team player that can work independently with minimal supervision.
Highly motivated, committed, self-starter and can adapt with changing priorities.

KPMG Ontario Pay Range Information

The expected base salary range for this position is $98,000 to $131,500 and may be eligible for bonus awards. The determination of an applicant’s base salary within this range is based on the individual’s location, skills, & competencies, and unique qualifications. In addition, KPMG offers a comprehensive and competitive Total Rewards program.

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best

Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity
, we do what is right | Excellence
, we never stop learning and improving | Courage
, we think and act boldly | Together
, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better
, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.

jobs.description:
Req Id:
432861

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Director, MEP & Electrical Infrastructure, you will provide strategic leadership for the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, power generation, and utility infrastructure programs that underpin Bell AI Fabric's national data centre platform. This role combines portfolio-level MEP governance with ownership of the electrical infrastructure ecosystem, including power generation, transmission interconnections, substations, distribution networks, backup power systems, and high-density cooling infrastructure.

You will establish the standards, delivery frameworks, procurement strategies, and technical governance that every site inherits and executes against. Working across engineering, construction, utilities, regulators, OEMs, and executive leadership, you will ensure the AI Fabric portfolio delivers scalable, resilient, and mission-critical infrastructure capable of supporting Canada's next generation of AI compute capacity.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Strategy

Own the enterprise-wide MEP and Electrical Infrastructure strategy across Bell AI Fabric's national data centre portfolio.
Establish standardized design bases, engineering specifications, technical standards, governance frameworks, and delivery playbooks across all sites.
Drive consistency, repeatability, scalability, and continuous improvement across multiple concurrent data centre developments.
Build and scale the MEP and Electrical Infrastructure leadership function as the program expands nationally.

Electrical Infrastructure & Energy Systems

Lead planning and execution of major electrical infrastructure programs supporting large-scale AI and data centre operations.
Establish technical requirements and design standards for HV and MV electrical systems, substations, switchyards, distribution networks, and critical power systems.
Oversee development of gas-fired generation assets, utility interconnections, backup power systems, and grid-connected energy infrastructure.
Lead utility negotiations, transmission access discussions, capacity planning, and interconnection agreements.
Develop long-term energy strategies to support portfolio growth while ensuring reliability, resilience, and operational continuity.
Evaluate and integrate emerging energy technologies including battery energy storage systems (BESS), microgrids, distributed generation, and grid modernization solutions.

MEP Engineering & Infrastructure Delivery

Define and govern MEP standards for power distribution, UPS systems, generators, cooling plants, chilled water systems, controls, and high-density/liquid cooling technologies.
Lead portfolio-wide modularization and prefabrication strategies to improve schedule certainty, quality, and scalability across sites.
Provide technical oversight and governance to site-level engineering, MEP, and construction leaders.
Ensure lessons learned, best practices, and engineering innovations are captured and implemented portfolio-wide.

Risk Management & Stakeholder Engagement

Lead program-wide risk identification, mitigation, change management, and issue resolution activities.
Manage relationships with regulators, utilities, EPC contractors, consultants, technology providers, and executive stakeholders.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on infrastructure strategy, energy planning, engineering governance, and program execution.
Influence and align multidisciplinary teams across Engineering, Procurement, Program Controls, Asset Management, Construction, Operations, and AI Fabric leadership.

Critical Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related Engineering discipline.
Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation strongly preferred.
PMP, PgMP, commissioning certification (CxA, ACG), or equivalent professional credential considered an asset.
15+ years of leadership experience delivering large-scale MEP, electrical infrastructure, energy, industrial, mission-critical, or hyperscale data centre programs.
Demonstrated success leading portfolio-level engineering, infrastructure, or capital programs valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Significant experience supporting gas-fired generation facilities and large-scale energy infrastructure.
Proven experience establishing technical standards, governance frameworks, and delivery playbooks across multiple facilities or programs.
Experience developing and scaling modular or off-site construction strategies for mission-critical infrastructure.
Strong knowledge of commissioning methodologies, FAT/SAT processes, integrated systems testing, and operational readiness programs.
Experience leading utility negotiations, transmission access discussions, and regulatory engagement.
Strong command of program cost management, forecasting, and integrated scheduling tools such as Primavera P6.
Exceptional executive presence with the ability to influence senior leaders, technical stakeholders, utilities, regulators, and industry partners.
Demonstrated ability to build, mentor, and scale high-performing engineering and infrastructure organizations.
Willingness to travel nationally between project sites, utility partners, fabrication facilities, and Bell AI Fabric locations.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

KPMG Corporate Finance Inc. is the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC)-regulated entity through which KPMG LLP provides investment banking services in Canada. KPMG Corporate Finance services are principally comprised of merger, acquisition and divestiture services and financing services, including raising debt and equity capital. We offer independent financial advisory and investment banking services to both private and public companies.

With over 100 professionals across Canada and a global network of 3,000+ bankers in 160 offices, we combine local execution expertise with global reach. KPMG Corporate Finance is consistently ranked the #1 mid-market investment bank in Canada.

As an experienced Associate Vice President, Corporate Finance, you will report to our Vice Presidents and Managing Directors. You are a self-starter who has an interest in mergers and acquisitions and capital markets and will bring your experience to deliver transactions for our clients.

Collaborative team player that can work independently with minimal supervision.
Highly motivated, committed, self-starter and can adapt with changing priorities.

new_jobs.description:
Req Id:
432861

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell’s AI Fabric initiative is pioneering a secure, sovereign AI compute network across Canada. This transformative portfolio includes seven large-scale, high-density data centres, anchored by a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2GW flagship site in Regina, Saskatchewan.

As Director, MEP & Electrical Infrastructure, you will provide strategic leadership for the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, power generation, and utility infrastructure programs that underpin Bell AI Fabric's national data centre platform. This role combines portfolio-level MEP governance with ownership of the electrical infrastructure ecosystem, including power generation, transmission interconnections, substations, distribution networks, backup power systems, and high-density cooling infrastructure.

You will establish the standards, delivery frameworks, procurement strategies, and technical governance that every site inherits and executes against. Working across engineering, construction, utilities, regulators, OEMs, and executive leadership, you will ensure the AI Fabric portfolio delivers scalable, resilient, and mission-critical infrastructure capable of supporting Canada's next generation of AI compute capacity.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership & Strategy

Own the enterprise-wide MEP and Electrical Infrastructure strategy across Bell AI Fabric's national data centre portfolio.
Establish standardized design bases, engineering specifications, technical standards, governance frameworks, and delivery playbooks across all sites.
Drive consistency, repeatability, scalability, and continuous improvement across multiple concurrent data centre developments.
Build and scale the MEP and Electrical Infrastructure leadership function as the program expands nationally.

Electrical Infrastructure & Energy Systems

Lead planning and execution of major electrical infrastructure programs supporting large-scale AI and data centre operations.
Establish technical requirements and design standards for HV and MV electrical systems, substations, switchyards, distribution networks, and critical power systems.
Oversee development of gas-fired generation assets, utility interconnections, backup power systems, and grid-connected energy infrastructure.
Lead utility negotiations, transmission access discussions, capacity planning, and interconnection agreements.
Develop long-term energy strategies to support portfolio growth while ensuring reliability, resilience, and operational continuity.
Evaluate and integrate emerging energy technologies including battery energy storage systems (BESS), microgrids, distributed generation, and grid modernization solutions.

MEP Engineering & Infrastructure Delivery

Define and govern MEP standards for power distribution, UPS systems, generators, cooling plants, chilled water systems, controls, and high-density/liquid cooling technologies.
Lead portfolio-wide modularization and prefabrication strategies to improve schedule certainty, quality, and scalability across sites.
Provide technical oversight and governance to site-level engineering, MEP, and construction leaders.
Ensure lessons learned, best practices, and engineering innovations are captured and implemented portfolio-wide.

Risk Management & Stakeholder Engagement

Lead program-wide risk identification, mitigation, change management, and issue resolution activities.
Manage relationships with regulators, utilities, EPC contractors, consultants, technology providers, and executive stakeholders.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on infrastructure strategy, energy planning, engineering governance, and program execution.
Influence and align multidisciplinary teams across Engineering, Procurement, Program Controls, Asset Management, Construction, Operations, and AI Fabric leadership.

Critical Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related Engineering discipline.
Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation strongly preferred.
PMP, PgMP, commissioning certification (CxA, ACG), or equivalent professional credential considered an asset.
15+ years of leadership experience delivering large-scale MEP, electrical infrastructure, energy, industrial, mission-critical, or hyperscale data centre programs.
Demonstrated success leading portfolio-level engineering, infrastructure, or capital programs valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Significant experience supporting gas-fired generation facilities and large-scale energy infrastructure.
Proven experience establishing technical standards, governance frameworks, and delivery playbooks across multiple facilities or programs.
Experience developing and scaling modular or off-site construction strategies for mission-critical infrastructure.
Strong knowledge of commissioning methodologies, FAT/SAT processes, integrated systems testing, and operational readiness programs.
Experience leading utility negotiations, transmission access discussions, and regulatory engagement.
Strong command of program cost management, forecasting, and integrated scheduling tools such as Primavera P6.
Exceptional executive presence with the ability to influence senior leaders, technical stakeholders, utilities, regulators, and industry partners.
Demonstrated ability to build, mentor, and scale high-performing engineering and infrastructure organizations.
Willingness to travel nationally between project sites, utility partners, fabrication facilities, and Bell AI Fabric locations.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.
